f859014f05e7.doc: compute-QA: are the computations and witnesses sound?
f859014f05e7.title: compute-QA: are the computations and witnesses sound?
f859014f05e7.content: Process_ComputeQA · strict (defaulted) · 6 step(s) . Run qou’s compute-QA gates over computations/ and its witnesses, and publish one verdict per gate to the qa-reports branch. WHY ONE PROCESS. The gates used to live as inline steps in four workflow files, so nothing named them as a set, and the order an agent ran them in locally was whatever it remembered. They are now one table (scripts/compute-qa.py) and this one diagram; the workflows call the table, and each step carries a # bpmn-node: back-reference here. THE COMMANDS DID NOT CHANGE. Each gate runs the exact command the workflow step ran, with the same exit-code handling: a strict gate fails on a non-zero exit, a warn or advisory gate never fails the run and its output is the report; when it exits non-zero its verdict is WARN rather than PASS, so a finding is not recorded as green. Measured on main before the move and after it, every gate’s exit codes and output are identical. QA IS AGENT-OWNED; CI IS A BACKUP. These workflows are dispatch-only (owner directive 2026-06-30, Actions billing), and several have never run. So the normal way through this process is an agent running python3 scripts/compute-qa.py before it commits, not CI. The lane says who runs a gate, not where. THREE OUTCOMES. A gate whose script cannot start (a missing module or binary) is UNKNOWN and never a pass. A failing self-test fails its gate whatever the gate’s mode, because a detector that has stopped matching its known positive reports everything clean. VERDICTS ARE NOT COMMITTED. Each gate writes test/results/compute-qa/<gate>.json, which is gitignored and is the layout bun run qa:publish reads. No rendered diagram — run bun run cat render:bpmn.

382800255962.title: Steps
382800255962.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Precision gates (NO-FLOAT64 family)Task_Precision | Gate runner (an agent before commit, or CI on dispatch) | — | Gates mpf-float-source, import-time-dps, never-raises-dps, float64-padding, mpf-context-dps, module-const, raw-float64 (strict, each with its self-test) and no-free-parameter (warn). From witness-staleness.yml. | . | Staleness and anchor gatesTask_Staleness | Gate runner (an agent before commit, or CI on dispatch) | — | Gates staleness-report (warn), q0-anchor-flip, q0-value-drift and authors-note-coverage (strict). From witness-staleness.yml. | . | LP/SDP dual gatesTask_LpDual | Gate runner (an agent before commit, or CI on dispatch) | — | Gates lp-dual-backend (the MPFR LP binary must be built first), pyhecke-tests and lp-dual-wired (strict), and lp-dual-survey (advisory). From lp-dual-gate.yml. | . | Probe float64 entry pointsTask_Probe | Gate runner (an agent before commit, or CI on dispatch) | — | Gates probe-float64-diff (strict, on the changed .py files) and probe-float64-survey (advisory). From probe-float64-gate.yml. | . | Braid-word provenanceTask_Words | Gate runner (an agent before commit, or CI on dispatch) | — | Gates word-provenance-selftest and word-provenance-diff (strict) and word-provenance-survey (advisory). From word-provenance-gate.yml. | . | Publish verdicts to qa-reportsTask_Publish | Gate runner (an agent before commit, or CI on dispatch) | — | Publish test/results/compute-qa/*.json with bun run qa:publish, keyed by commit. The verdicts are derived, so they go to the orphan qa-reports branch and are never committed. | .

8d52d990c6c5.content: A skill states the capability; this Tool is one way to exercise it. Each skill’s declared input and output contract follows, where it has one. compute-integration-watcher . Cross-layer wiring auditor — watches for newly-landed formal/analytic improvements (proofs, propositions, lemmas, axiom→theorem upgrades, witness data) on the default branch AND on open PRs, and checks whether each one has been wired into the production compute chain. e920c04efa3b.title: Tools — qou
e920c04efa3b.content: The Tool nodes qou declares in its tools graph — one instance’s slice of every instance’s tools. As an API: OpenAPI document · MCP tool list · API reference. A skill states a capability generically: what an actor needs to know to perform a task. A Tool is one concrete way to exercise it, with an installation, an invocation and typed inputs and outputs. One skill may be satisfied by several tools, and one tool may satisfy several skills. They are separate graphs and this is the tools one. The relation between them is satisfies, and it runs from a tool to a skill — this tool is one way to do that, never this skill is a tool. 245Tool nodes 4skills satisfied 245invoked as a shell command 0reachable over MCP

0807951a693e.content: The Tools of every layer, in the two forms other tools read: . | openapi.json — OpenAPI 3.1.0, one operation per Tool. The paths are the Tools’ call contracts, not HTTP endpoints: each operation’s x-invoke says how the Tool is really reached. | mcp-tools.json — the answer an MCP server gives to tools/list: each tool’s name, description and input schema, read from the registrar that serves it. | .

eaf05b438bb5.doc: Is the generated Lean in sync with its generators?
eaf05b438bb5.title: Is the generated Lean in sync with its generators?
eaf05b438bb5.content: Process_LeanRegenerateAndDiff · strict (defaulted) · 2 step(s) . Check that the Lean text a script in this repository writes is still exactly what that script writes. Two files carry such text: every knot block of QOU/Knot/GeneratedGluing.lean (from scripts/gen-gluing-lean.py) and the depth-3 corner column BokutShiaoCornerDepth3 in UGB/GrobnerShirshov/HeckeCompletion.lean (from scripts/gen-hecke-corner-column.py 3). WHY IT IS STRICT. These are proofs. If a generator and its output part company, a Lean file that compiles is carrying certificates nothing in the repository produces, and the next regeneration silently changes a proof. The check is cheap (about nine seconds) and writes nothing, so strictness costs nothing. THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO. A generator that cannot run, most often because SnapPy is not installed, is UNKNOWN and never reported as in sync. That is the parity rule the witness-parity Tool already follows. WHAT IS NOT CHECKED, AND WHY. The depth-2 column BokutShiaoCorner (section 4ad) was written by hand first; the generator was checked against it by re-deriving the same words and rules, not the same text. Measured 2026-10-05, the two differ on 964 lines while proving the same thing, so a textual diff there would report drift that is not drift. The module header of GeneratedGluing.lean and its closing end line are hand-written too, and are excluded from the comparison for the same reason. DRIFT IS A DECISION, NOT A FIX. When the regenerated text differs, either the generator changed (and the Lean should be regenerated) or the Lean was edited by hand (and the generator should learn the edit, or the edit should go). Which one is right is a judgement about a proof, so it goes to the author; the agent does not overwrite either side. No rendered diagram — run bun run cat render:bpmn.

de2b1907b5c5.title: Refresh computation witnesses
de2b1907b5c5.content: Process_WitnessRefresh · strict (defaulted) · 6 step(s) . Bring qou’s computation witnesses back in line with the producers that write them, without a witness ever being rewritten that the owner did not approve. Owner, 2026-10-04: “all witnesses tools will need to go into the KG”; this is the process those Tools run in. A WITNESS IS CONTENT HERE. Its numbers are what the paper quotes, so the owner’s rule that a migration changes no mathematics applies to it, and so does the ask-first rule for refreshing one. That is why the decision sits in the owner’s lane between the measurement and the re-run, and why nothing before it writes a file: the dry run and the parity check both work on the committed tree or a scratch copy of it. THE PLAN IS run_pipeline.py --dry-run --content-only, UNCHANGED. The process does not re-derive staleness; it calls the pipeline’s own answer through the witness-refresh-plan Tool, so the list a person approves is exactly the list the pipeline would act on. No rendered diagram — run bun run cat render:bpmn.
